title: Breaking Up Is Hard To Do
gist: A short teaser (paywalled full piece) arguing that despite years of US-China effort to cut technological reliance on each other, entrenched two-way dependencies persist across a wide swath of sectors, and new dependencies keep emerging even as old ones are severed.

themes.theme: US-China tech decoupling proves harder than intended

insights.claim: Despite both China and the US devoting intense effort to cutting their technological reliance on each other, the overall lesson is that decoupling is really difficult, with only some impact achieved so far.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Investors should discount narratives of clean, rapid US-China tech supply-chain separation; positioning for full decoupling is likely to be premature.
insights.quote: These efforts have had some impact, but the overall lesson is that decoupling is really difficult.

insights.claim: Entrenched, often two-way, US-China dependencies persist across biotech, robots, semiconductors, optical transceivers, medical devices, lidar sensors, solar inverters, gas turbines, batteries and electricity grid equipment.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: This is the watchlist of sectors where supply-chain risk from geopolitics remains structurally high rather than resolved, relevant to hedging or sourcing decisions in these industries.
insights.quote: The list of sectors with entrenched (and often two-way) dependencies includes biotech, robots, semiconductors, optical transceivers, medical devices, lidar sensors, solar inverters, gas turbines, batteries and electricity grid equipment.

insights.claim: New US-China tech dependencies keep emerging even as old ones are cut, driven by the complementarity of American demand and innovation with Chinese manufacturing efficiency and scale, persistent talent flows, and the fact that China's own technological progress makes its high-end tech companies more dependent on specialized US inputs.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Counterintuitively, as Chinese tech firms advance up the value chain they may need more, not fewer, specialized US inputs, undercutting bets on near-term Chinese tech self-sufficiency.
insights.quote: And even as old dependencies are cut, new ones pop up.
insights.locator: even as old dependencies are cut
